diagram_math_checks.justification: Example and proof 1.2 fix A=(0,0), B=(1,0), P=R_1^(0)=(1/2,0), Q=R_1^(1)=(1/2,1). Orange traces A-P-B and cyan traces A-Q-B. Coordinates and common scale match these data; both endpoints and both interior images are included (filled dots).

Proof 1.2: |A-P|=|P-B|=1/2 and |A-Q|=|Q-B|=sqrt(1/4+1)=sqrt(5)/2. Proof 2.1: the nearest reference point to Q on {(t,0):0<=t<=1} is P, hence distance 1. The vertical dashed guide is shortened only to avoid the dots; the label records the full point-to-reference distance.

V=0 gives gradient zero by proof 1.1. Both algorithms use the nonzero centered chord B-A=(1,0); the NEB supplier centered-chord tie branch applies because all energies agree. Equal adjacent lengths kill the ordinary NEB spring term and string spacing residual, exactly as in 1.2. No force arrows suggest a nonzero force.

Each discrete chain has three vertices and two undirected segments, with endpoint degrees 1 and interior degree 2. The rendered union has four vertices and four chain segments (straight baseline visibly contains P), including the explicit right cyan edge Q-B and complete baseline A-B. No cycle syntax is used. These are discrete chains, not smooth MEPs; the Remarks say this explicitly. All rigorous arguments remain unchanged and independent of the figure.
